questions.answer: A systematic error shifts repeated measurements consistently in the same direction, so its cause should be identified and corrected, for example by a zero check or calibration. A random error varies unpredictably between readings and produces scatter, so repeated readings and a mean can reduce its effect.
accepted_alternatives: Equivalent descriptions of a shared bias and unpredictable scatter with one physically suitable response to each
questions.tolerance: Both error patterns and both matched responses are required for full marks.

marking_points.text: States that a systematic error shifts repeated measurements consistently in the same direction
Gives a suitable response to systematic error, such as checking zero, calibrating or correcting the identified cause
States that a random error varies unpredictably between readings and produces scatter
Gives repeated readings and calculation of a mean as a suitable response to random variation

questions.answer: The calipers distinguish 0.1 mm. They are most suitable for the 124 mm rod because 124 mm is within their 150 mm range and their resolution is the required 0.1 mm. The micrometer is most suitable for the 0.60 mm wire because the diameter is within its 25 mm range and its resolution is the required 0.01 mm. Fine resolution shows the smallest distinguished change, not closeness to the true diameter, so it does not by itself establish accuracy.

questions.answer: The mean indicated reading is 24.87 g and the range is 0.02 g. The balance resolution is 0.01 g. The readings are precise because their range is small, but not accurate because their mean is 0.48 g above the true value. The +0.48 g empty reading is a positive systematic zero error. Subtracting it gives a corrected mean of 24.39 g. This restores accuracy for the reference mass but leaves the 0.02 g range, and therefore the precision, unchanged.
accepted_alternatives: Correct each reading by 0.48 g first, then calculate the same corrected mean and range
questions.unit_policy: All numerical mass values and resolution require g.
questions.tolerance: Mean, range, zero correction and corrected mean are exact to 0.01 g.

marking_points.text: Calculates the mean indicated reading as 24.87 g
Calculates the range of the indicated readings as 0.02 g

parts.label: (b)
parts.answer: The resolution is 0.01 g. The readings are precise because their range is only 0.02 g. They are not accurate because their mean of 24.87 g is 0.48 g above the true value of 24.39 g.
accepted_alternatives: Equivalent measurement-quality judgements supported by the calculated data
parts.tolerance: Each judgement must use its correct comparison.

marking_points.text: States the balance resolution as 0.01 g
Identifies the readings as precise because their range is only 0.02 g
Identifies the uncorrected readings as not accurate because their mean of 24.87 g is 0.48 g above the true value

parts.label: (c)
parts.answer: The +0.48 g empty reading is a positive zero error and therefore a systematic error because the same upward shift affects every reading. Corrected mean = 24.87 g - 0.48 g = 24.39 g. The corrected mean equals the true value, so accuracy improves. Subtracting the same value from every reading leaves their range at 0.02 g, so precision is unchanged.
accepted_alternatives: Correcting every reading separately and obtaining the same 24.39 g mean and 0.02 g range
parts.unit_policy: The zero reading, corrected mean and range require g.
parts.tolerance: Exact correction and a correct distinction between accuracy and precision are required.

Subtracts 0.48 g from 24.87 g to obtain the corrected mean of 24.39 g
Explains that the correction restores accuracy to the true value but leaves precision unchanged because the 0.02 g range is unchanged
